quote_text:
Thoroughly deserved three points. First  half I wasn't too happy. I thought we were,  
um, a bit pedestrian on the ball.  Aberdeen never threatened us,  
so yeah I was a bit frustrated. Half-time I  made a change, I wanted a few more runners  
from midfield to give Aberdeen some  problems. And then when we done that,  
we caused them all sorts of problems and I  thought in the end, um, we ran over the top  
of Aberdeen. Just disappointed it was only four  — I thought it could have been more. But look,  
it's been far too long. Seven games without a  win. Just happy to get that, that victory finally.
What does it mean to you to get that box?
Yeah I'm happy. I am. Of course  I'm happy. The players are happy,  
and hopefully the supporters are happy  with the second half performance.
Did you see in that second half, Barry,  what this team can be like when it—
Yeah. And I see when they listen as well. They  can be a good team. As I said back to the game  
last Sunday, their commitment and attitude’s  always been really good for me. I can never  
label that against them. It’s just the quality  at times. So we worked really hard during the  
week on things that we can get better at.  And it was just nice to see things, um,  
happen that you happen when you work with things  on the training ground. But I had to remember at  
half-time — we need to be better, guys. We need  to threaten Aberdeen. And once we got that first  
goal, I felt there was a calmness about us and we  started to play the way that I know the boys can.
When you see a team run over the top as you  said there, does it almost give you a bit  
of frustration of what you know could have  came before if they reached those heights?
Yeah. Look, I tend not to look in the past.  Look, it’s not been good enough this season.  
It’s been way off it. Um, I've come in  and I’ve tried to change it. One thing  
I've changed is the attitude of the players —  it's been really good. There’s been a few bumps  
as I've always said. There’s certainly a lot  of good players in there, and they just need  
to make sure we finish the season strongly. And  then we'll take it from there, whatever happens.
Barry, that's 10 assists for Nico Raskin  this year. Six of them since you came in. Has  
that been a conscious effort from you to get him  further forward or is he just really enjoying his—
No, I think Nico will tell you he wants to be a  number six. I think he can be a number six. But  
also I think he needs to add different attributes  to his game. I think he can play further forward.  
Um, and it’s good to have that flexibility.  We've had a few arguments, shall we say. Um,  
but I don’t mind that. He’s a good boy. He’s  got really good ability, there’s no doubt.  
And I think certainly for the turn of the year  his levels of performance have been up there.
Few arguments about yourself?
Yeah. Too much of myself, that's  why I argue with him. But he's got  
an opinion. I don't mind people with  opinions. I just think if he works,  
um, on things that we speak about, um,  he’s got a real chance playing at the top.
Is he someone the team should be looking to build—
I didn’t hear you.
Is he a player that they should  build the team around next?
I'm not going to get into that. And it's just  — I don’t know his contract situation or… I'm  
just going to enjoy these last couple  of games managing and coaching Nico.
Were you surprised by how Aberdeen  approached that? As you say they  
didn’t really touch Rangers  at all that whole 90 minutes.
Um, no. They came to frustrate us, that’s what  I felt. They had a lot of men behind the ball.  
I kinda thought that would be the way they would  approach it. But obviously they’re still going  
for third place. I did mention that. They’ve  still got a cup final to play. But I just…  
I thought in the first half they were there for  the taking. That’s the thing — it frustrated me  
a wee bit. But listen, we took things on  board that I spoke about at half-time and,  
um, I thought honestly we ran over  the top of them in the second half.
Last couple of guys — you made a change  at half. But do you expect more from…
Yeah, I expect more from everybody. 'Cause I'm  demanding. And they might look at me and they  
might say, “Oh there he goes again,” but that’s  just the type of person I am. I’ll try and get  
everything I can out of players. Some players  might not like it, some will like it. But I'm not  
going to stand there — I know they're a brilliant  football club and I’m going to make sure I try and  
get every single ounce I can possibly out of  every single player. And it’s not just about  
Nadem. Nadem’s got really good qualities.  He just found it tough today. And again,  
it's one of the ones — you have to make decisions.  And I made a decision. And I thought, you know,  
just Hamza… I thought the other boys that  came on have gave me a problem. I want to  
have a problem. I've not had a problem for a  long time. So I've got a problem now — what  
starting eleven I'm going to have to pick,  um, against Sunday night and Wednesday night.
Last two guys. Barry, what's  the situation with Oscar Cortés?
It’s a fitness thing. I've told you — you  asked me the question a couple of weeks ago  
about Oscar and about Danny. I look at people  when they train. And I have to make decisions.
So will Oscar get an opportunity  before the end of the season?
Maybe. Danny has had an opportunity — that’s  more like Danny when I seen him coming on. Um,  
but it’s not just about Danny and Oscar. But  everybody keeps asking about them. There’s  
a lot of players that are not getting much game  time. But you need to earn your right to play. You  
just don’t play for the sake of playing. You have  to earn the right to be — certainly on my team.
Last one. Stevie?
Barry, can I just ask you about Bailey Rice?
Yes.
When he came on, he was effortless. Looked really  
classy on the ball. In terms of Rangers  maybe progressing forward in years to come,  
wanting that number six — that was spoke  about quite a lot at the start of the  
season. Where do you see him? Because you  did say he was behind in his development.
Yes. You see him taking strides. And do you think  
that he can be the player  that you think he can be?
Yes. I think he can. He can be a number six for  Rangers. Again, I get asked quite a lot — “Why you  
not playing him?” I don’t think he’s ready to play  every single game. Now Bailey will say otherwise,  
which I have no problem with. But he’s got  all the attributes that’s needed for me to  
play in that position. He has to work  on things. And one thing I will say  
about Bailey — and Connor’s the same,  Nico’s the same, Dills the same — they  
really tune in and listen and understand  they need to get better at certain things.  
So this next five days I’ll continue to  work with Bailey. And hopefully in the  
future we’ll see Bailey be a Rangers number six,  because he certainly has the ability to do that.
Thanks guys.
How far away is he from being  that player that can start?
Yeah. He just needs a bit of work. So  that would be a pre-season. He should,  
in my opinion, have been playing more  regular before I came. But as I said,  
I think he’s behind in development and  needs to work on things. And certainly  
it’s something that we’ve been speaking about,  we’ve been working on, and he’s been tuning in.  
And that’s all you can ask from a young player  — who everybody knows I think highly of him.
title: "We need to be better!" Barry Ferguson Post Match Press Conference | Rangers 4-0 Aberdeen
